'''Teri W. Odom''' is an American chemist and materials scientist. She is the chair of the chemistry department, the Joan Husting Madden and William H. Madden, Jr. Professor of Chemistry, and a professor of [[materials science and engineering]] at [[Northwestern University]].<ref name=advocate/><ref name=cen/> She is affiliated with the university's [[International Institute for Nanotechnology]], Chemistry of Life Processes Institute, Northwestern Initiative for Manufacturing Science and Innovation, Interdisciplinary Biological Sciences Graduate Program, and department of applied physics.<ref name=advocate/><ref name="4. Northwestern University Chemistry"/>

==Education==
Odom attended [[Stanford University]], where she earned a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in chemistry, was elected to [[Phi Beta Kappa]], and received the Standford's Marsden Memorial Prize for Chemistry Research (1996). She obtained her PhD in [[chemical physics]] from [[Harvard University]] in 2001 under the guidance of [[Charles M. Lieber]], then conducted post-doctoral research at Harvard with [[George M. Whitesides]] from 2001 to 2002.<ref name=star>{{cite web|url=https://chicagoacs.starchapter.com/images/downloads/Chemical_Bulletin/2004_01_chembull.pdf|title=CHICAGO SECTION AMERICAN CHEMICAL SOCIETY Regular Monthly Meeting|date=2004-01-23|publisher=Chicago Chapter, American Chemical Society|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref><ref name="4. Northwestern University Chemistry">{{cite web|title=Teri W Odom|url=http://www.chemistry.northwestern.edu/people/core-faculty/profiles/teri-odom.html|publisher=Northwestern University Department of Chemistry|access-date=May 14, 2014}}</ref>

== Career ==
Odom joined Northwestern University's department of chemistry in 2002<ref name=star/> and became the department chair in 2018.<ref name=advocate/> In 2010, she became the founding chair of the Noble Metal Nanoparticles Gordon Research Conference<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grc.org/noble-metal-nanoparticles-conference/2010/|title=2010 Noble Metal Nanoparticles Conference GRC|website=www.grc.org|language=en|access-date=September 17, 2018}}</ref><ref name=packardorg/> Between 2016 and 2018, she was associate director of the [[International Institute for Nanotechnology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iinano.org/teri-odom|title=Teri Odom {{!}} International Institute for Nanotechnology|website=www.iinano.org|access-date=August 28, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170731213549/http://www.iinano.org/teri-odom|archive-date=2017-07-31}}</ref><ref name=advocate>{{cite web|url=https://www.optica-opn.org/home/career/2018/august/teri_odom_on_being_an_advocate/|title=Teri Odom on Being an Advocate|last=Robinson|first=Rebecca|date=2018-08-21|publisher=OPTICA|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref> Odom has worked on the editorial advisory boards of ''[[ACS Nano]]'',<ref name=dod/><ref name=editorinchief/> ''[[Bioconjugate Chemistry]]'', ''[[Materials Horizons]]'', ''[[Annual Review of Physical Chemistry]]''<ref name=editorinchief/> ''Natural Sciences'', ''[[Nano Futures]]'', and ''[[Accounts of Chemical Research]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} Odom became an inaugural associate editor for [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s ''[[Chemical Science (journal)|Chemical Science]]'' journal in 2009, a position she held until 2013.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2014/sc/c3sc90050a|title=Chemical Science editorial|journal=Chemical Science|year=2014|volume=5 |issue=5|pages=18–20|doi=10.1039/C3SC90050A|access-date=2023-04-24|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="4. Northwestern University Chemistry"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://eipbn.org/plenary-speaker-1/|title=Teri W. Odom|publisher=Electron, Ion and Photon Beam Technology and Nanofabrication|date=2021-11-18|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref> She was on the editorial advisory board of ''[[Nano Letters]]'' beginning in 2010 and became editor-in-chief in 2019.<ref name=cen/><ref name=editorinchief>{{cite press release|url=https://www.acs.org/pressroom/newsreleases/2019/november/acs-names-teri-w-odom-as-the-new-editor-in-chief-of-nano-letters.html|title=American Chemical Society names Teri W. Odom as the new editor-in-chief of Nano Letters|date=2019-11-07|publisher=American Chemical Society|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref> In 2013, she became a founding Executive Editor for ''[[ACS Photonics]]''.<ref name=dod/><ref name=editorinchief/>

== Research interests ==
Research in the Odom group focus on controlling materials at 100&nbsp;nm scale and investigating their size and shape-dependent properties. Odom group has developed parallel, multi-scale pattering tools to generate hierarchical, anisotropic, and 3D hard and soft materials with applications in imaging, sensing, wetting and cancer therapeutics. As a result of Odom's nanofabrication tools, she has developed flat optics that can manipulate light at the nanoscale and beat the diffraction limit and tunable plasmon-based lasers. Odom also conducts research into nanoparticle-cell interactions using new biological nanoconstructs that offer imaging and therapeutic functions due to their shape (gold nanostar).<ref name=cen/><ref name=advocate/><ref name=packardorg/>

[[File:Scientist Teri Odom Cottrell Conference 2026.jpg|thumb|upright=0.75|
Odom at the 2026 Cottrell Scholars Conference in [[Tucson]]]]

== Personal life ==
Odom's husband Brian, now a physicist and astronomer at Northwestern University, piqued her interest in science by introducing her to the [[double-slit experiment]] while they were dating. He encouraged her to pursue undergraduate summer research, an experience that inspired her to continue studying physics and chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://inchemistry.acs.org/acs-and-you/eminent-scientist-teri-odom.html|title=Eminent Scientist Teri Odom Talks about Her Journey to the Brilliant Science of Thinking Small|last=Tinnesand|first=Michael|date=2019-03-15|publisher=InChemistry|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.northwestern.edu/newscenter/stories/2009/10/odom.html|title=Husband and wife Packard Fellows|last=Fellman|first=Megan|date=2009-10-15|publisher=Northwestern University|access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref>
